/.title: CREMA — Brand Guidelines Manual
/.description: Living editorial brand manual and design system for CREMA, crafted as a portfolio case study by Proiectum Studio.
h2: Crema serves bold espresso, velvety cappuccinos, and slow-baked pastries in a space that feels warm¹, grounded², and easy³ to return to.
p: This manual defines the visible language for Crema: a neighbourhood espresso bar built around slow evenings, bold roasts, and unhurried daily rituals.
Reserve roast tin: hot-stamped copper foil sits lightly on fibrous cream cotton stock over warm travertine.
Use this index to move through the assets, rules, and production notes that keep Crema consistent across café, print, packaging, and digital touchpoints.
Crema is an espresso bar for bold coffee, velvety cappuccinos, and slow moments of pause. The brand feels warm, grounded, tactile, and quietly confident.
1 Warm: timber, amber light, and hospitality built for unhurried evenings.
2 Grounded: honest roasts, tactile paper, and colour drawn straight from the bar.
3 Easy: every sign, label, and cup stays readable and effortless to reproduce.
The Crema logo is the primary signature. It should feel sculpted soft-serif curves, while applied with disciplined spacing, contrast, and scale.
Primary Crema logo artwork on a steamed-milk paper field for window posters, social headers, and seasonal pours.
Use the full Crema logo on shopfronts, menus, packaging, and first-contact materials.
Keep the logo white on dark or gradient artwork, and roasted espresso or ink black on pale café materials.
Do not redraw the script, add drop shadows, stretch the letterforms, or trap it inside a badge.
The palette carries the café’s twilight warmth: steamed milk neutrals, warm cedar timber, caramel crema glow, and deep roasted-espresso contrast.
The core palette is drawn from café materials: warm cedar timber rafters, steamed milk foam, golden caramel crema, and dark espresso depth. Use exact values for print and digital production.
Gradients are atmospheres, made of two blended colours.
Gradients are campaign atmospheres for posters, social stories, menu specials, and seasonal pours. Keep the logo white and allow generous negative space.
Window poster: the white Crema logo floats over an amber dusk gradient for warm evening street visibility.
Campaign poster: deep roasted espresso fades into warm cedar timber with one crisp drink headline.
Use warm neutrals as the largest field, roasted espresso for contrast and appetite, warm timber for architectural depth, and caramel crema as a warm evening accent.
HEX and RGB define screen appearance. CMYK and Pantone are production targets for menus, stickers, cups, signage, and packaging; proof before release.
Typography balances espresso-bar warmth with a disciplined manual system. Display type brings presence; mono notes keep production information exact.
Use display type for drink names, posters, and menu moments that should feel warm and appetising.
Do not mix in extra decorative fonts; the logo already carries the handmade character.
Typography should make menus easy to scan, prices easy to compare, and the Crema voice recognisable at counter distance.
Body copy should sound like a seasoned barista host: warm, clear, specific, and never over-written.

Close-up texture is our key expression. We shoot drinks near enough to read their surface — crema, microfoam, ice, the layers where espresso meets milk — so the photograph sells the craft before the logo arrives.
Iced cold brew shot shows translucent amber layers and crystal ice.
The drink’s own roast layers do the work
Texture frame — golden crema and micro-bubble detail are the signature photographic expression of our brand.
Applications should feel physical and tactile: cotton menus, checkered roast boxes, handheld cups, canvas awnings, posters, and dusk interiors.
Tactile cotton menu — 320gsm sheet with brass corner clip, ceramic demitasse, kouign-amann, and debossed pulp coaster.
Parlour service — checkered roast gable box, fluted glass, and brass tray in dusk light.
Street poster: café specials should look useful and present, not like generic campaign advertising.
Evening poster: warm timber light and restrained white type invite regulars in after dusk.
Roast & pastry boxes — Warm Timber checkerboard stock and debossed cotton labels.
Handheld takeaway cup: sculpted crema wordmark wraps warm Steamed Milk stock against sunlit ceramic tiles.
Storefront signage: woven Warm Timber canvas awning and hanging blade banner over fluted dusk glass.
